Anr on 17 August, 2023
 In The High Court At Calutta

Court No. 551

 Mangali Bhakta & Ors.
 Vs.
 The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Anr.
 Mr. Pingal Bhattacharya,
 Mr. Poonam Keswari
 ......for the appellants-claimants.

Mr. Rajdeep Bhattacharya
 ...........for the respondent no. 1-insurance Co.
The Deficit Court Fee is paid.

The instant appeal has been preferred against the judgment dated 24th December, 2019 passed by the learned Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, 1st Court, Tamluk, Purba Medinipur in MAC Case No. 701 of 2015.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, 1st Court, Tamluk, Purba Medinipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The brief fact of the case is that the present appellants being the claimants filed an application before the learned tribunal under Section 166 of the M.V. Act for getting compensation on the ground that their predecessor was died in a road traffic accident due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle duly ensured under the policy of the respondent insurance company.

The learned tribunal is heard the matter and after taking the evidences both oral and documentary allowed the compensation in favour of the claimants to the tune of Rs. 5,29,000/- alongwith interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filling of the claim case.
The claimants being aggrieved by the said judgment has preferred this instant appeal for enhancement of the award.
Learned advocate for the appellants submitted before this court that the impugned award passed by the learned tribunal is not at all correct.
The notional income of the deceased was calculated as Rs.3,000/- per month which is not proper.

The deceased was a Poller and used to earn Rs.7,000/-
per month.

He also argued that the future prospects was not considered in this case and learned tribunal has committed error for not following the guideline of the Hon'ble Apex Court passed in Pranay Sethi so he prayed for just and proper compensation.

sentences.text: Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the insurance company submitted before this court that the impugned award passed by the leaned tribunal suffered no illegality.
The observation of the learned tribunal regarding income of the deceased is quite justified.
No document of income was produced by the claimants in this case for which the learned tribunal has calculated the income of the deceased notionally to be Rs. 100/- per day.
He also pointed out that the observation of the learned tribunal regarding future prospects need be verified.
Heard the learned advocate perused the materials; it appears that the sole ground of income of the deceased is under challenged.

Learned tribunal has considered the income of the deceased notionally to be Rs. 3,000/- as there is no documentary evidences before the learned tribunal regarding monthly income of the deceased, I find no infirmity in the impugned order for fixing the income of the deceased notionally.

However, this is the practice adopted by this court on regular occasions when the accident was occurred on the year 2015 and upwards the notional income of the deceased should be Rs.5,000/-
per month.
On that score, the observation of the learned tribunal appears to be not correct.

The learned tribunal has not also considered the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court passed in Pranay Sethi wherein it has been specifically observed that in a case under Section 166 of the M.V. Act the claimants are entitled to the future prospects on the establish notional income.
In this case the establish notional income of the deceased is calculated Rs. 5,000/- per month.
Thus the claimants are entitled to get the future prospects to the tune of 40% of his establish income.
Considering the age of the deceased to be 26, the applicable multiplier of this case would be 17.
Considering the entire aspect the impugned award passed by the learned tribunal is hereby modified.

The just and proper compensation is as follows:-
1.Monthly Income ......................................Rs.5,000/-
2. Annual Income.....................................Rs.60,000/-

6. Add: General damages.....................Rs.70,000/-

sentences.text:
2 Amount already paid..................Rs. 5,29,000/- Balance........................................Rs. 6,12,000/-
The appellants are entitled to get the balance compensation amounting to Rs.6,12,000/- alongwith interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of this case i.e. from 04.12.2015 within eight weeks through the office of the learned tribunal in the name of the claimants vide four equal account payee cheques.

The cheque in the name of the minor claimant no. 2 shall be receive by claimant no. 1 being her natural guardian of mother and the claimant no. 1 shall deposit the same in a fixed deposit scheme under a nationalized bank so that the amount can be utilized by the claimant no. 2 after attaining her majority.
On such deposit the claimants are entitled to get the compensation as mentioned above according to the prevalent rules subject to the ascertainment of payment of requisite court fees.

It appears that the learned tribunal has passed the award subject to the fact that after such award be satisfied; the insurance company is at liberty to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

At this juncture, it is necessary observe that the insurance company shall recover the entire amount alongwith the balance amount from the owner of the offending vehicle according to the direction of the Hon'ble Apex Court passed in Swaran Singh and Challa Bharathamma.
The instant FMA is disposed of.
All connected applications, if any, stand disposed of.
Interim orders, if any, stand vacated.
Parties to act upon the server copy and urgent certified copy of this order be provided on usual terms and conditions.

(Subhendu Samanta, J.)
